LAREDO, Texas — Gabriel Adolfo Gonzalez was arrested Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 11:33 a.m., and booked into the Webb County Jail on an alleged second-degree felony charge of robbery, according to Webb County booking records.

The Webb County Sheriff's Office made the arrest, the records show. Gonzalez was booked into the county jail on the single felony charge.

No bond had been set on the charge as of the booking record reviewed by Webb Watch 956.

A second-degree felony in Texas is punishable by two to 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000.

An arrest is an allegation, not a conviction. Gabriel Adolfo Gonzalez is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

Update — October 22, 2026

Court records reviewed by Webb Watch 956 on the Webb County Odyssey public-access portal show the October 22 warrant was tied to revocation proceedings in Gonzalez's robbery case, 2025CRH000469D2, filed in the 111th District Court on April 9, 2025. The state's application to adjudicate his probated sentence was filed September 24, 2026, and a judge signed an order to revoke with capias on September 28. A motion-to-revoke arraignment hearing is set for 9:00 a.m. on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, reset from an earlier October 29 date.

The same record shows Gonzalez pleaded guilty to the robbery count on November 10, 2025, and received deferred adjudication with six years of community supervision and 120 hours of community service (4:1 credit); the aggravated-assault-with-a-deadly-weapon and drug-possession counts in that case were dismissed. Deferred adjudication is not a conviction under Texas law. An arrest is an allegation; Gonzalez is presumed innocent of the underlying allegations unless proven guilty.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff's Office Booking Jail Search; Webb County public-access court records.

Webb Watch 956
